Processing and Visualising Flow Data

10.1 Overview

Spatial interaction represents the flow of people, material or information between locations in a geographical space. It encompasses everything from freight shipments, energy flows, global trade in rare antiquities, flight schedules, rush hour woes and pedestrian foot traffic.

Each spatial interaction, as an analogy for a set of movements, is composed of a discrete origin/destination pair. Each pair can be presented as a cell in a matrix where rows are related to the locations (centroids) of origin while columns are related to locations (centroids) of destination. Such a matrix is known as an origin/destination (OD) matrix or spatial interaction matrix.

In this hands-on exercise, I will build an OD matrix by using the Passenger Volume by Origin Destination Bus Stops data set downloaded from LTA DataMall.

By the end of the hands-on exercise, I would have:

  • imported and extracted OD data for a selected time interval,

  • imported and saved geospatial data (i.e. bus stops and mpsz) into sf tibble data frame objects,

  • populated planning subzone code into bus stops sf tibble data frame,

  • constructed desired lines in the geospatial data from the OD data, and

  • visualised passenger volume by origin and destination bus stops by using the desired lines data.

10.2 Getting Started

Before we start, we will need to install and load the necessary R packages into the R environment:

  • sf for importing, integrating, processing and transforming geospatial data.

  • tidyverse for importing, integrating, wrangling and visualising data.

  • tmap for creating elegent and cartographic quality thematic maps.

  • stplanr provides functions for solving common problems in transport planning and modelling such as downloading and cleaning transport datasets; creating geographic “desire lines” from origin-destination (OD) data; route assignment, locally and interfaces to routing services such as CycleStreets.net; calculation of route segment attributes such as bearing and aggregate flow; and ‘travel watershed’ analysis.

  • DT provides an R interface to the JavaScript library DataTables. R data objects (matrices or data frames) can be displayed as tables on HTML pages, and DataTables provides filtering, pagination, sorting, and many other features in the tables.

pacman::p_load(sf,tidyverse,tmap,stplanr, DT, XML, xml2)

10.3 Preparing the Flow Data

10.3.1 Importing the OD data

The code chunk below uses read_csv() of readr package to import the Passenger Volume by Origin Destination Bus Stops dataset as a tibble data frame into the R environment:

odbus <- xmlParse("data/aspatial/PassengerVolumeByOriginDestinationBusStops.xml")
Note
skip

Number of lines to skip before reading data. If comment is supplied any commented lines are ignored after skipping.
